purpose: Track what Japanese vowel-sequence evidence has been recovered, what can be used directly in Formant Canvas, and what must not be presented as an empirical trajectory.

studies.population: Japanese adults; male and female values reported separately for relevant contextual conditions
sequences: within-word VV (pooled contextual vowel targets; not sequence-specific continuous trajectories)
studies.measurement_structure: Published numeric tables contain contextual vowel targets and timing/transition summaries rather than normalized-time F1/F2 point series for individual /VV/ sequences.
studies.normalization: Use the publication's reported Hz summaries as published; no synthetic normalization is introduced by this manifest.
studies.current_canvas_use: Adult Japanese VV presets use pooled within-word contextual F1/F2 targets and reported timing proportions; F3 is borrowed from Kasuya et al. (1968), and the continuous transition is modeled by Canvas.
studies.blocker: No sequence-specific normalized-time F1/F2 numeric trajectory series has been recovered from this source.
studies.notes: The existing Canvas values can be traced to the published tables, but they must not be relabeled as a measured continuous trajectory.

studies.study: Zhang (2022), Prosodic Influences on the Acoustics of Vowel Sequences
studies.population: Japanese speakers in a prosodic-boundary experiment; the dissertation also analyzes other languages
studies.measurement_structure: Dynamic F1/F2 trajectories are analyzed with GAMM over the central 20%-80% portion of the tautosyllabic vowel sequence.
studies.normalization: As specified in the dissertation's analysis; the manifest does not reconstruct curves from model summary statistics.
studies.current_canvas_use: Qualitative support only; not used as a numeric trajectory preset.
studies.blocker: The dissertation figures and GAM/GAMM summary tables establish dynamic trajectories, but a reusable per-timepoint Hz series or fitted-model object from the dissertation experiment has not been recovered.
studies.notes: The author's Time_series_data_tutorial does contain genuine pointwise F1/F2/F3 files, but its single tutorial recording with ai/au/ou and t1-t4 labels does not match the dissertation's Japanese ae/ai/au x word/list/IP-final multi-speaker design. Do not substitute that tutorial dataset for the dissertation experiment. Do not digitize plotted dissertation curves and call the resulting points source measurements.

studies.population: A public tutorial recording; speaker population is not documented as the dissertation Japanese cohort
studies.measurement_structure: Pointwise time-series formant files are publicly available; vowels_ait.txt, vowels_aut.txt and vowels_out.txt contain measured-time columns and 30 indexed samples per labeled token in the inspected ai file.
studies.normalization: Raw Hz formant values are present in the tutorial text files; the tutorial demonstrates subsequent analysis/plotting in R.
studies.current_canvas_use: None. Retained only as a public example of Zhang's time-series extraction/data format.
studies.blocker: The tutorial recording/design does not match the dissertation Japanese experiment: it uses ai/au/ou in one public vowels.wav/TextGrid with t1-t4 labels rather than ae/ai/au across word-final/list-final/IP-final conditions and a documented Japanese speaker cohort.
studies.notes: This is useful for reproducible extraction-format research but must not be promoted as a normative Japanese VV trajectory or as Zhang (2022) dissertation data without independent provenance establishing that identity.

studies.study: Sun & Hayashi (2025), Acoustic, Auditory and Articulatory Analysis of Vowel Sequences in Japanese by Chinese Learners
studies.population: 7 native Japanese speakers (4 female, 3 male) plus 19 advanced Chinese learners of Japanese
studies.measurement_structure: Each vowel sequence is divided into 19 equal temporal intervals, yielding 20 formant measurement points.
studies.normalization: Lobanov-normalized formant values are used in the reported trajectory analysis/plots.
studies.current_canvas_use: Qualitative validation only; not used as a group numeric trajectory preset.
studies.blocker: The article reports the 20-point measurement procedure but the plotted example trajectories are not a reusable native-speaker group numeric table; no public supplementary CSV was recovered in the checked locations.
studies.notes: A single plotted native speaker (JM1) can be described as a single-speaker illustration, but should not be promoted to a normative adult Japanese group trajectory.
